t: Virgil shaped scattered older tales of Aeneas into a founding myth that tied Rome to Troy and the family of Julius Caesar to its heroes and gods.
The first six books follow the wanderings from Troy to Italy, after the Odyssey, and the last six the war in Latium, after the Iliad.
Unfinished at Virgil's death in 19 BCE, it was published on Augustus' order and became the basis of Latin education for centuries.
dyk: Virgil died with the poem unfinished and wished the manuscript burned; Augustus ordered his executors to disregard the wish and publish it with as few changes as possible. Its many half-complete lines and abrupt ending are read as signs that it was never finished.
ev: Greek vases already show accounts of Aeneas founding a new home in Etruria
Virgil dies at Brundisium with the poem unfinished; Augustus orders it published
The grammarian Maurus Servius Honoratus writes the most complete ancient commentary on the poem
Gavin Douglas completes his Eneados, the first full and faithful rendering in an Anglic language
Henry Purcell's opera Dido and Aeneas is performed
Ivan Kotliarevsky writes Eneida, a mock-heroic burlesque in the Ukrainian language

f.made: Virgil, Roman poet, under Augustus and with Maecenas as his patron; published after his death by his literary executors Lucius Varius Rufus and Plotius Tucca on Augustus' order
f.form: A Latin epic of 9,896 lines in dactylic hexameter, in twelve books of roughly 700 to 900 lines each, left unfinished
f.where: Read in printed editions and in translations into many languages
f.known: Arma virumque cano; Dido and Aeneas; the descent to the underworld; pietas and furor; the founding myth of Rome; Virgil as Dante's guide
